born.name: William Blake
bio: Born in Soho, London, the son of a hosier, he trained as an engraver and printed and hand-coloured his own illustrated books.
His Songs of Innocence and of Experience include The Tyger. Largely ignored in his lifetime, he is now counted among Britain’s greatest poets.
The words of the beloved hymn “Jerusalem” come from the preface to his poem Milton.

born.name: Nancy Mitford
born.short: The eldest – and wittiest – Mitford sister
bio: Born in London, she was the eldest of the famous Mitford sisters, whose eccentric upbringing she turned into comic gold.
The Pursuit of Love (1945) and Love in a Cold Climate (1949) became bestsellers and have been adapted for television more than once.
She settled in Paris after the war and later moved to Versailles, where she died in 1973.

born.name: Berry Gordy
born.short: The man behind the Motown sound
bio: Born in Detroit, the former boxer and car-factory worker borrowed $800 from his family in 1959 to start the label that became Motown.
Hitsville U.S.A. launched The Supremes, Stevie Wonder, Marvin Gaye, The Temptations and the young Michael Jackson.
Today he turns 97 – still the proud father of the “Sound of Young America”.

born.name: Randy Newman
born.short: You’ve got a friend in him
bio: Born in Los Angeles into a family of film composers, he made his name with wry, clever songs such as Short People and I Love L.A.
He wrote You’ve Got a Friend in Me for Toy Story and has won two Oscars, in 2002 and 2011.
This year, aged 82, he wrote the music for Toy Story 5.

born.name: Armando Iannucci
born.short: The mind behind The Thick of It
bio: Born in Glasgow, he helped create Alan Partridge on radio and then turned British politics into comedy with The Thick of It.
He went on to make Veep in America and the films The Death of Stalin and The Personal History of David Copperfield.
In 2026 it was announced that he will write the next Paddington film.

born.name: Karen Gillan
bio: Born in Inverness, she became a household name in 2010 as Amy Pond, the Doctor’s companion, alongside Matt Smith in Doctor Who.
Hollywood followed: she plays the blue-skinned Nebula in Guardians of the Galaxy and starred in the Jumanji films.
Next, she is due to appear with Henry Cavill in a new version of Highlander.

remembered.name: Washington Irving
remembered.short: Gave us Rip Van Winkle and Sleepy Hollow
bio: Born in New York City, he was the first American writer to win real fame in Europe.
While living in England he wrote Rip Van Winkle and The Legend of Sleepy Hollow, published in The Sketch Book in 1819–20.
He was also the first to call New York “Gotham”, and later served as the US Minister to Spain.

remembered.name: Enid Blyton
bio: Born in East Dulwich, London, she trained as a teacher before writing more than 600 books for children.
The Famous Five began in 1942, and Noddy and The Secret Seven followed in 1949.
Her stories of midnight feasts and ginger beer still sell in their millions around the world.

remembered.name: Leslie Nielsen
remembered.short: Surely the funniest straight face ever
bio: Born in Regina, Canada, he spent decades as a serious leading man, including in the 1956 science-fiction classic Forbidden Planet.
Then came Airplane! in 1980 and his deadpan delivery turned him into a comedy star.
As Frank Drebin in Police Squad! and The Naked Gun films, he kept a perfectly straight face to the end.

remembered.name: David Prowse
remembered.short: Darth Vader – and the Green Cross Code Man
bio: Born in Bristol, he became British heavyweight weightlifting champion and represented England at the Commonwealth Games.
His towering frame filled Darth Vader’s armour in the original Star Wars films.
To British children of the 1970s he was just as famous as the Green Cross Code Man, teaching road safety.

history.head: The Royal Society is born
history.body: After a lecture by Christopher Wren at Gresham College in London, twelve men agree to found a society for the study of science.

history.head: Beethoven’s Emperor
history.body: Beethoven’s Piano Concerto No. 5, the “Emperor”, has its first public performance at the Gewandhaus in Leipzig.

history.head: Women go to the polls
history.body: New Zealand holds the first national election in a self-governing country in which women can vote. More than 90,000 do so.

history.head: Lady Astor wins Plymouth
history.body: Nancy Astor’s victory in Plymouth Sutton is declared. Days later she becomes the first woman to take her seat in the Commons.

us: I’m Leaving It Up to You

sport.head: Everyone on the boundary
sport.body: England beat West Indies by 2 runs in Sydney after Mike Brearley sends every fielder – even the wicketkeeper – to the boundary.

sport.head: Sampras sees off Agassi
sport.body: Pete Sampras beats Andre Agassi 6-1, 7-5, 6-4 in Hannover to win his fifth season-ending ATP title.

sport.head: Fury shocks Klitschko
sport.body: In Düsseldorf, Tyson Fury outpoints Wladimir Klitschko to become the world heavyweight champion.

sport.head: Vardy’s record run
sport.body: Jamie Vardy scores against Manchester United – a goal in 11 Premier League games in a row, a new record.

• 1893 – New Zealand women vote in a general election, a world first
• 1919 – Nancy Astor wins Plymouth Sutton and soon becomes the first woman to take her seat in the Commons
